catalog.label: Instrument-air low-pressure indication at RHOB receiving header P-R triggered alarm AL-44 and paused work.
catalog.detail: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored.

catalog.label: Utilities air gallery serves RHOB process area; local indication P-R normally shows normal pressure band.
catalog.detail: The Utilities air gallery distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. The receiving header H-R at RHOB has a local indication point P-R that typically displays within a normal operating range (above 5.0 bar).

catalog.label: Alarm AL-44 activates when P-R pressure drops below 4.5 bar and clears above 5.0 bar.
catalog.detail: The RHOB PLC low-pressure input from point P-R (AL-44) is configured to trigger a 'COMP FAULT' indication if the measured pressure falls below 4.5 bar, and it resets when pressure rises above 5.0 bar.

catalog.label: At 10:00 AM, P-R pressure dropped from ~6.8 bar to below alarm thresholds (<4.5 bar).
catalog.detail: RHOB operations detected an instrument-air low-pressure indication at the receiving header (P-R), dropping from approximately 6.8 bar to a value that triggered the AL-44 alarm.

catalog.label: Work package WO-527-E field execution record was blank at folder issue.
catalog.detail: The work package cover indicates the temporary instruction attachment field and the field execution record (WO-527-E) were both left blank when issued, meaning no specific instructions or updated drawings were attached to guide boundary preparation.

catalog.label: Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time (boundary preparation incomplete).
catalog.detail: The work package cover explicitly states that the maintenance acceptance signature field had not been filled in when the incident occurred, indicating the boundary preparation phase was incomplete or unverified by receiving operations.

catalog.label: No evidence confirms whether crew saw recent changes or used a different version of the equipment-location sheet.
catalog.detail: The training extract does not state which configuration drawing the crew (U-A/U-B) viewed, nor is there any record that either person received a briefing on recent service-routing changes affecting the instrument-air system.

catalog.label: No documented confirmation of understanding regarding root cause assessment or response steps.
catalog.detail: The provided evidence does not contain any record showing that the crew understood how to assess a low-pressure alarm, what immediate actions were required beyond pausing work, or who was responsible for restoring service safely.

catalog.label: Shift log records 'boundary preparation in progress' but does not identify point of interruption or valve states.
catalog.detail: The shift entry at 09:48 notes that the crew was at the gallery with boundary preparation underway, yet it provides no information about which valves were open/closed, whether isolation procedures had been completed, or where exactly in the distribution system the pressure loss originated.
